title: Shortwave capacity overlay: policy for transient capacity, graduated throttles, and invoice smoothing
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: Customers on Dedicated occasionally need short, high-throughput windows (e.g., marketing pushes, nightly batch jobs). Existing surge pools provide headroom but have produced surprising invoices and abrupt throttles. Goal: define a lightweight 'Shortwave overlay' policy that grants short-lived capacity boosts, enforces graduated throttles, and applies invoice-smoothing caps to avoid customer surprises while protecting multi-tenant fairness.

Scope: policy + runtime knobs + billing rules + rollout playbook for Dedicated fleet only. Not covering Dedicated private on-prem upgrades (separate follow-up).

Objectives:
- Define shortwave window semantics: max duration, replenishment cooldowns, and per-tenant burst budget accounting.
- Ensure throughput guarantees for pinned capacity remain unaffected; shortwave should be excess/headroom only.
- Implement graduated throttles: soft degradation (queueing/priority-bump) before hard 429s.
- Bill only measured overage beyond shortwave allowance with an invoice cap/notification for first offending month.
- Provide operator visibility and automatic remediation hooks (disable shortwave per-tenant, emergency reclaim).

Acceptance criteria:
- API surface for tenant admins to opt-in/out and set max shortwave multiplier (1.0-3.0).
- Runtime enforces: shortwave_max_duration=15m default, cooldown=120m, per-tenant budget meter in tokens, reclaimed when idle.
- Throttle ladder implemented: (1) prefetch KV cache warming and background batching; (2) progressive request delay with priority tags; (3) soft 429 with Retry-After and friendly invoice notice; (4) hard 429 after configurable grace.
- Billing: first month overage subject to auto-cap equal to 50% of projected overage invoice and one proactive email; subsequent months billed normally. Cap and email are configurable by finance via feature flags.
- Observability: three dashboards (shortwave usage, per-tenant debt, throttle events) and two alerts (sustained shortwave >70% capacity for 10m; per-tenant overage >X USD/day).

Constraints and trade-offs:
- Conservative default duration to limit backend pressure but adjustable for high-trust enterprise tenants.
- Cap introduces accounting complexity and potential revenue delay; product/finance signed off on 50% cap for first month to improve retention.
- Requires KV-cache pre-warming heuristics to avoid tail-latency regressions during shortwave activation.
comments: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with PM (Sofia Mendes), Finance (Liam Ortega), and Infra (Priya Nair). Agreed to prototype with 15m default and 120m cooldown. Action: infra to produce a simulation by 2026-02-19. - Aisha

2026-02-18: Simulation results from infra: shortwave multiplier 2.0 yields 18% increase in token cost under realistic traces; tail p95 latency increases by 12% without KV prewarm. Decided to add prewarm path and progressive throttle. - Marcus

2026-02-22: Design review with runtime team. Chose 'queued-priority' ladder: tag requests during shortwave as 'shortwave' -> enter soft queue with credit-based dequeue. Implemented a per-tenant credit bucket emitted to metrics. PR scaffold created. - Marcus
2026-02-28: Finance accepted invoice smoothing proposal (first-month cap at 50%). Product requested opt-in toggle in Console and an audit log entry for any capped invoice. - Sofia

2026-03-03: Security reviewed for audit and found no PII exposure. KMS billing metadata must be included in logs; security_review_required set to false but audit log requirement added. - Security (Elena)
